title: Storage — Separate ordinary database connections from initialization and migrations
body:
## Problem and intended outcome

Ordinary reads currently enter the same database-opening function as schema preparation. Make connection ownership explicit: a normal operation opens an already prepared database; creation, migration and recovery stay with their supported lifecycle owners. Failures during connection setup must release any handle already created.

Coordination: #1209. Related product/operability owner: #1212. Suggested implementation order: **1**.

## Current source evidence

Source audit baseline: [`52f8b278bad5ddd8c261af127dca712cdd8da925`](https://github.com/hynk-studio/augnes/commit/52f8b278bad5ddd8c261af127dca712cdd8da925), rechecked on 2026-10-10 KST. The source findings below were inspected through GitHub; this registration did not reproduce runtime failures or run Local Canonical. Main integration is distinct from installed-runtime adoption.

- [openDatabase()](https://github.com/hynk-studio/augnes/blob/52f8b278bad5ddd8c261af127dca712cdd8da925/lib/db.ts#L238-L285) creates the parent directory, opens with `fileMustExist: false`, configures the connection, then executes legacy/research migrations and current schema preparation before returning.
- [GET /api/vnext/continuity-pins](https://github.com/hynk-studio/augnes/blob/52f8b278bad5ddd8c261af127dca712cdd8da925/app/api/vnext/continuity-pins/route.ts#L39-L71) calls this function and closes only the returned handle in `finally`.
- If setup throws after construction but before return, the caller has not received the handle. The opener has no local cleanup guard. This identifies a missing cleanup path; an actual resource leak was not reproduced in this audit.
- Existing [canonical migration coordination](https://github.com/hynk-studio/augnes/blob/52f8b278bad5ddd8c261af127dca712cdd8da925/scripts/canonical-database-migrations.mjs) and [runtime database bootstrap/recovery](https://github.com/hynk-studio/augnes/blob/52f8b278bad5ddd8c261af127dca712cdd8da925/scripts/runtime-database-bootstrap.mjs) are the starting owners to inspect. A duplicate initialization framework is not the goal.

An already migrated database may incur checks without schema changes. The finding is responsibility coupling, not a claim that every GET changes schema.

## Proposed bounded change

1. First make exception-safe ownership explicit for every failure after a handle is created, preserving the useful original failure.
2. Inventory ordinary readers/writers, startup, CLI, tests, installation, upgrade and restore callers. Distinguish deliberate initialization from ordinary connection use.
3. Separate ordinary connection from directory/file creation and migration. Reuse supported lifecycle preparation, with an explicit and actionable refusal for missing, incompatible or unprepared databases.
4. Keep schema-readiness checks read-only. Preserve necessary per-connection configuration. Choose interfaces from current callers; the function names above are evidence, not a prescribed API.

Keep this separate from changes to table layout, semantic fingerprints, record formats, scoring policy or the storage engine.

## Acceptance

- [x] Inject failures at meaningful post-construction setup stages; every owned handle is closed and the original failure remains diagnosable.
- [x] A normal read of a prepared disposable database creates no database/directory and invokes no migration or schema-preparation path; persisted schema and logical records remain unchanged.
- [x] Missing or incompatible preparation yields a distinct failure without creating an empty database or repairing it implicitly from GET.
- [x] Supported explicit initialization, nonempty upgrade and restore/restart still work through their lifecycle owners; preserve existing recovery and refusal behavior.
- [x] A supported subsequent write still preserves project isolation, stale/replay refusal and transaction atomicity.
- [x] Callers and tests distinguish preparation from normal access; document the new ownership and compatibility behavior without introducing an additional operator ceremony for ordinary use.

Use disposable fixtures. Do not test this by mutating the installed production store.

## Verification and status

Completed by [PR #1440](https://github.com/hynk-studio/augnes/pull/1440), merged into `main` on **2026-10-11 10:33:32 KST** (2026-10-11 01:33:32 UTC). Merge commit: [`36e0902308cd8844ab52881fd2e9ab48e6157dd0`](https://github.com/hynk-studio/augnes/commit/36e0902308cd8844ab52881fd2e9ab48e6157dd0). GitHub merge state was rechecked for this closeout on 2026-10-11 KST.

The acceptance checklist is completed against the merged implementation and the acceptance evidence recorded in #1440:

- Exception-safe synchronous/asynchronous ownership covers configuration, readiness, explicit preparation and backup failures; cleanup refusal retains both failures and is not falsely reported as a released handle.
- Prepared, nonempty ordinary reads and the real continuity-pins GET perform no directory creation or schema preparation, preserving schema, records, database bytes and files.
- Missing, unprepared, incompatible and unavailable storage is distinguished; GET refuses safely without creation or repair, and replacement database images are checked again.
- Canonical initialization, nonempty supported upgrades, backup/restore/restart and recovery/refusal behavior remain with existing lifecycle owners.
- Subsequent writes preserve project isolation, stale/CAS and existing replay behavior; fault injection after a real revision update verifies transaction rollback.
- Callers, fixtures, packaging and ownership documentation were updated without adding a manual setup step to normal startup.

**Recorded verification:** final candidate `cf0c62318c12f86556102338fd248c1470c1d490`, tree `da4f6e0c9ec513779e0d21c10054e2b6885b30eb`, base `ca8dbda6575c4150767238bf9230fea3e317bae0`; Local Canonical selected `full-canonical`, with all **16 phases PASS**. The PR records receipt validation as `valid_deciding_evidence=true`, `status=valid`, `issues=[]`, and final cleanup with 0 remaining owned processes. Earlier failed candidates and their corrections remain documented in the PR.

**Evidence boundary:** this closeout reconciles the merged PR and its recorded verification; it did not rerun tests after merge. Installed-runtime adoption, production-store migration, deployment/release and real-provider execution were not performed. This closes only the bounded storage-ownership work in #1436; it does not close the broader #1209/#1212 work or the separate #1437 task.

Original implementation guidance (retained for provenance): before implementation, re-inspect current source, callers, relevant active owners and AGENTS.md. Use behavior-owned focused checks and the current Local Canonical planner for the final exact candidate where required. Preserve failed attempts and report skipped checks and their reasons. Registration creates no installation, production migration, deployment, provider-use or merge authority.
